To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nitrendipine (a calcium channel blocker) did not block synaptic transmission or long-term potentiation in hippocampus.

the organic calcium channel blocking agents--nitrendipines, verapamil and flunarizines--and micromolar concentrations (10 microM) of diazepam, are ineffective in antagonizing long term potentiation in the guinea pig hippocampus.

nitrendipine and the benzodiazepepines diazepam, flunarizin and verapamil are ineffective in blocking synaptic transmission, and in preventing the development of LTP, suggesting that the calcium channel blockers are not useful tools in studying the pre- and postsynaptic calcium mechanisms in LTP.
